sentence: NHS pages on vitamins and minerals describe getting what the body needs from a balanced diet, with supplements recommended only for some people and times of year.

sentence: Vitamin D is the main example, because it is difficult for people to get enough from food alone.

sentence: The NHS says everyone should consider a daily 10 microgram vitamin D supplement in autumn and winter.

sentence: NHS England starts this seasonal advice at age 4, while NHS inform in Scotland starts it at age 5.
note: Seasonal advice starts at age 4 in England, 5 in Scotland

sentence: Some groups are advised to take it all year: people who are not often outdoors, such as those who are frail or housebound or living in care homes, people who usually cover most of their skin outdoors, and people with dark skin from African, African-Caribbean or South Asian backgrounds.
note: Groups all year: not often outdoors, frail, housebound, care homes, cover most of skin, dark skin African, African-Caribbean, South Asian

sentence: For breastfed babies the NHS advises a daily vitamin D supplement throughout the year, and children aged 1 to 4 are also advised to take it year-round.
note: Breastfed babies from birth to 1 year daily supplement; children 1 to 4 10 micrograms throughout the year

sentence: Healthy Start vitamin products are free for eligible families.
note: Healthy Start vitamin products free for eligible families

sentence: Anyone who is pregnant or could become pregnant is advised to take a 400 microgram folic acid supplement every day until the twelfth week of pregnancy.
note: 400 microgram folic acid daily until 12 weeks pregnant

sentence: The NHS says some people need a higher dose, for example those with diabetes or taking medicine for epilepsy, and that this is arranged with a doctor.
note: Some need higher dose 5mg, e.g. diabetes, epilepsy medicine; speak to your doctor first

sentence: For vitamin D, the NHS says taking more than 100 micrograms a day could be harmful, and this applies to adults, pregnant and breastfeeding women and children aged 11 to 17.
note: Not more than 100 micrograms (4,000 IU) a day as could be harmful

sentence: For folic acid, the NHS says too much could be harmful, but 1 milligram or less a day is unlikely to cause any harm.
note: 1mg or less a day unlikely to cause any harm

sentence: The NHS guide to vitamins and minerals covers vitamins A, B, C, D, E and K, folic acid, calcium, iodine and iron.
note: NHS guide covers vitamins A, B and folic acid, C, D, E and K, plus calcium, iodine and iron

sentence: For vitamin A and for iron, the NHS says most people can get all they need from a varied and balanced diet.
note: Vitamin A: should be able to get all you need by varied and balanced diet; iron same

sentence: The NHS says vitamin D helps regulate the amount of calcium and phosphate in the body, and that sunlight is the main source.
note: Vitamin D helps regulate calcium and phosphate; sunlight main source

sentence: It says that from about late March or early April to the end of September most people can make all the vitamin D they need from sunlight on the skin.
note: From late March/April to end of September majority make all vitamin D they need from sunlight

sentence: Iron is important for making red blood cells, which carry oxygen around the body.
note: Iron important in making red blood cells which carry oxygen

sentence: Liver is very rich in vitamin A, and the NHS says liver or liver products such as pâté should not be eaten more than once a week.
note: Liver very rich in vitamin A; do not eat liver or liver products such as pate more than once a week
